reports.title: Kenya National Budget FY 2026/27 Breakdown: KES 4.82 Trillion Expenditure, Revenue & Deficit Gap
reports.seoTitle: Kenya National Budget 2026/2027: KES 4.82T Treasury Breakdown | Budget Ndio Story
reports.seoDescription: Authoritative analysis of Kenya's FY 2026/27 KES 4.82T national budget: KRA ordinary revenue (KES 2.99T), debt servicing (KES 1.20T), and county equitable share (KES 502B).
reports.author: Budget Ndio Story Research Desk

provenance.source: National Treasury Budget Statement FY 2026/27 & Parliament Appropriation Act 2026

citizenTakeaway: For every KES 100 collected by the government in taxes, approximately KES 40 is allocated strictly to service domestic and external public debt.
Education remains the largest single sector at KES 784.5 Billion, with over half going to Teachers Service Commission (TSC) salaries.
The 47 County Governments receive KES 502 Billion in total devolution transfers, comprising KES 428B unconditional equitable share and KES 74B in conditional grants.
The budget deficit of KES 1.15 Trillion (5.5% of GDP) will be funded predominantly through domestic borrowing (KES 1.03T) from local banks and pension funds.
reports.content:
### 1. The Macro-Fiscal Framework: Where Does the Money Come From?

Kenya’s FY 2026/27 National Budget stands at a record **KES 4.82 Trillion**. The revenue framework relies on three distinct pillars:

- **Ordinary Revenue (KRA Tax Receipts)**: **KES 2,985.7 Billion** (61.9% of the budget), anchored by Income Tax (PAYE and Corporate Income Tax) and Value Added Tax (VAT at 16%).
- **Appropriations-in-Aid (A.I.A)**: **KES 644.8 Billion** (13.4%), generated directly by state departments, public universities, and regulatory authorities through user fees and licenses.
- **Grants & Concessional Loans**: **KES 43.6 Billion** (0.9%) from bilateral development partners and multilateral facilities.
- **The Fiscal Deficit Gap**: **KES 1,146.2 Billion** (23.8%), which must be plugged through **KES 1,030.1 Billion in domestic market borrowing** and **KES 116.2 Billion in external sovereign financing**.

### 2. Tier-1 National Sector Allocations

The National Assembly approved the following sectoral allocations:

1. **Education**: **KES 784.5 Billion** (16.3% of total budget) — TSC salaries (KES 421.9B), HELB loans (KES 56.7B), Free Secondary capitation (KES 54.6B), and Junior Secondary School transition (KES 30B).
2. **Governance, Justice, Law & Order (GJLO)**: **KES 353.3 Billion** (7.3%) — National Police Service, Judiciary, and Independent Oversight Commissions.
3. **Public Administration & International Relations**: **KES 341.2 Billion** (7.1%).
4. **Health**: **KES 175.0 Billion** (3.6%) — Kenya Medical Supplies Authority (KEMSA), national referral hospitals (KNH, MTRH), and Primary Health Care funds.
5. **Agriculture & Rural Development**: **KES 62.4 Billion** (1.3%) — National Fertilizer Subsidies, CAIPs shared funding, and FLLoCA climate resilience.

### 3. What Happens to the Debt Service Obligation?

Kenya’s Consolidated Fund Services (CFS) ring-fences **KES 1,203.1 Billion** solely for public debt servicing (interest and principal redemptions). This mandatory constitutional obligation takes legal priority over all ministry spending, underscoring the tight fiscal space faced by the National Treasury.

reports.title: Kakamega County FY 2026/27 Fiscal Review: KES 19.45B Allocation, Healthcare (33.2%) & Sugar Belt Roads
reports.seoTitle: Kakamega County Budget 2026/2027: KES 19.45B Allocation & Projects | Budget Ndio Story
reports.seoDescription: BNS Mashinani field review of Kakamega County's KES 19.45B budget. Healthcare (33.2%), sugar belt road tarmacking, and own-source revenue performance.
reports.author: BNS Mashinani Western Region Desk

provenance.source: Kakamega County Annual Budget Estimates FY2026/27 & COB Implementation Report

citizenTakeaway: Kakamega County receives KES 19.45 Billion, placing it 4th nationally in equitable share behind Nairobi, Kiambu, and Nakuru.
One-third (33.2%) of the county budget is dedicated to Health Services, centered on staffing rural health centres and operationalizing Level 4 sub-county hospitals.
Infrastructure and agricultural access roads receive 34.0% of the development envelope, specifically targeting cane transportation corridors in Butere, Mumias, and Malava.
Own-Source Revenue (OSR) collection reached KES 1.85B against a KES 2.20B target, representing an 84% revenue efficiency rating.
reports.content:
### 1. County Overview: Balancing Scale and Service Delivery

Kakamega County is home to over 1.8 million residents across 12 sub-counties and 60 wards. Under the CRA 3rd Basis Formula, Kakamega was allocated **KES 19,450.7 Million** in equitable revenue share.

### 2. Sectoral Allocation Priorities

- **Health Services (33.2% / KES 6.45B)**: Construction of sub-county mortuaries, primary health care commodity supply, and stipend support for 2,400 Community Health Promoters.
- **Transport & Public Works (34.0% / KES 6.61B)**: 10km of gravel-to-bitumen road upgrades per sub-county and drainage culverts across the sugar belt.
- **Agriculture, Livestock & Fisheries (18.7% / KES 3.64B)**: Subsidized farm inputs (certified maize and tea seeds), artificial insemination kits, and fish farming ponds in Lurambi and Ikolomani.
- **Education & Vocational Training (14.1% / KES 2.74B)**: County bursary fund (KES 240M across wards) and polytechnic infrastructure modernization.

### 3. BNS Mashinani Field Verification Findings

Our field trackers verified that the Kakamega Level 6 Teaching & Referral Hospital has achieved 78% civil works completion, though delays in specialized radiology equipment procurement remain a bottleneck.

faqs.answer: Kakamega County was allocated KES 19.45 Billion in equitable share from the National Treasury, ranking 4th among all 47 counties.

faqs.answer: Infrastructure and Roads (34.0%) and Healthcare (33.2%) represent over two-thirds of Kakamega County's entire budget, followed by Agriculture (18.7%) and Education (14.1%).

reports.title: Kilifi County Fiscal Review: KES 16.89B Devolution Share, UHC & Blue Economy Investments
reports.seoTitle: Kilifi County Budget 2026/2027: KES 16.89B Blue Economy & UHC | Budget Ndio Story
reports.seoDescription: BNS Mashinani analysis of Kilifi County's KES 16.89B budget: artisanal marine fisheries, cashew nut revival, UHC worker grants, and Ganze water pipelines.
reports.author: BNS Mashinani Coast Region Desk

provenance.source: Kilifi County Fiscal Strategy Paper & County Assembly Appropriation Act

citizenTakeaway: Kilifi County receives KES 16.89 Billion in equitable share, supporting an economy spanning coastal tourism, artisanal fishing, and arid hinterlands.
The county committed KES 4.10 Billion (24.3%) to Agriculture and Blue Economy, focusing on cold storage at landing beaches and modern motorized boat gear.
Universal Health Coverage grants provide KES 340M in co-funding for coastal dispensaries in Magarini, Kaloleni, and Malindi.
Drought resilience projects in Ganze sub-county absorbed KES 580M for water pan desilting and solar borehole pumping.
reports.content:
### 1. Geographical Realities & Fiscal Balancing

Kilifi County faces a dual economy: a thriving coastal tourism and marine belt alongside drought-prone inland pastoralist zones in Ganze and Magarini. The **KES 16.89 Billion** allocation reflects this dual mandate.

### 2. Key Investment Pillars

- **Blue Economy & Agriculture (24.3%)**: Modernization of Ngomeni and Kichwa cha Kati fish landing sites, seaweed farming grants in Kibokoni, and cashew nut seedling distribution.
- **Health Services (29.2%)**: Upgrades to Malindi Sub-County Hospital maternity wing and distribution of anti-malarial commodities.
- **Water Infrastructure (18.5%)**: Reticulation of Baricho water supply pipelines to underserved villages.
- **Roads & Transport (31.4%)**: Rural access road grading and beach access infrastructure.

faqs.answer: Kilifi County receives KES 16.89 Billion in unconditional equitable share from the national government for FY 2026/2027.

faqs.question: What is Kilifi County's primary agricultural and economic focus?
faqs.answer: Kilifi focuses on the Blue Economy (marine fisheries cold chain and motorized boat subsidies), cashew nut/coconut revival, and water pipelines in drought-prone inland areas.

reports.content:
### 1. Nakuru County's Fiscal Powerhouse

As Kenya's newest city and agricultural hub, Nakuru operates with a budget of **KES 22,180.4 Million**. It achieves the highest execution efficiency (93.5%) in the region.

### 2. Industrial & Agricultural Value Chain Focus

- **County Aggregation & Industrial Parks (CAIPs)**: Construction of cold storage warehouses at Egerton and Naivasha to eliminate post-harvest potato and vegetable losses.
- **Health Modernization (34.8%)**: Operationalization of the Nakuru Level 5 Oncology Center and sub-county maternity theatres in Molo, Gilgil, and Subukia.
- **Geothermal Direct Use**: Pilot agro-processing projects utilizing Olkaria geothermal steam for crop drying and milk pasteurization.

reports.title: Where Does Every 100 Shillings Go? Servicing Kenya's KES 1.20 Trillion Public Debt Obligation
reports.seoTitle: Kenya Public Debt Servicing 2026/27: KES 1.20T CFS Obligation | Budget Ndio Story
reports.seoDescription: Investigative analysis of Kenya's public debt servicing: domestic interest payments, Eurobond maturities, and the fiscal squeeze on essential civic services.
reports.author: Wanahabari Data Journalism Team

provenance.source: National Treasury Public Debt Statistical Bulletin & Central Bank of Kenya Weekly Bulletins

citizenTakeaway: Kenya will spend KES 1.20 Trillion on public debt service in FY 2026/27, exceeding the entire development budget of the national government.
Over 75% of the debt servicing obligation is domestic interest paid to local commercial banks and institutional bondholders.
Heavy domestic government borrowing crowds out private sector credit, keeping SME loan interest rates above 16%.
Under Article 214 of the Constitution, public debt charges are directly charged to the Consolidated Fund and cannot be voted down by Parliament.
reports.content:
### 1. The Anatomy of Kenya’s KES 1.20T Debt Bill

Public debt servicing has grown to become the single largest expenditure block in the national budget. In FY 2026/27, the National Treasury has earmarked **KES 1,203.1 Billion** under Consolidated Fund Services (CFS).

### 2. Domestic vs External Squeeze

- **Domestic Debt Servicing (KES 910B)**: Interest on Treasury Bills and Fixed-Rate Treasury Bonds.
- **External Debt Servicing (KES 293B)**: Bilateral loans, multilateral facilities (World Bank, IMF, AfDB), and commercial sovereign debt amortization.

### 3. The Civic Implication

Because debt is a non-discretionary constitutional charge, any shortfall in KRA tax collection immediately results in budget cuts to education capitation, health supplies, and county equitable share disbursements.

faqs.question: How much does Kenya spend on debt servicing each year?
faqs.answer: In FY 2026/27, Kenya allocates KES 1.20 Trillion to debt servicing, consuming approximately 40.3% of all ordinary tax revenue collected by the KRA.

faqs.question: Why can Parliament not reduce the debt servicing budget?
faqs.answer: Under Article 214 of the Kenyan Constitution, public debt service is a statutory charge on the Consolidated Fund, meaning it must be paid automatically without legislative alteration.

reports.seoTitle: Kenya Education Budget 2026/2027: KES 784.5B TSC, HELB & Capitation | Budget Ndio Story
reports.seoDescription: Comprehensive analysis of Kenya's KES 784.5B Education Budget: TSC teacher salaries (KES 421.9B), HELB loans (KES 56.7B), and Junior Secondary CBC capitation (KES 30B).

provenance.source: National Treasury Budget Estimates: Vote 1064, Vote 1065, Vote 1066 & TSC Act Appropriation

citizenTakeaway: Education is Kenya's largest national sector at KES 784.5 Billion, accounting for 16.3% of all government spending.
Over half (54%) of the education budget goes directly to teacher salaries under the Teachers Service Commission (KES 421.9B).
The Higher Education Loans Board (HELB) receives KES 56.7 Billion under the new student-centered university funding model.

reports.content:
### 1. Education as the Pillar of Human Capital

Kenya’s **KES 784.5 Billion** education envelope is distributed across four primary state departments:

- **Teachers Service Commission (TSC)**: **KES 421.9 Billion** (53.8%) for 400,000+ primary, secondary, and JSS teachers.
- **State Department for Basic Education**: **KES 154.2 Billion** (Free Primary and Day Secondary capitation, school feeding).
- **Higher Education & Research**: **KES 128.4 Billion** (HELB loans, University Fund scholarships, TVET construction).
- **Vocational & Technical Training (TVET)**: **KES 38.0 Billion** (Dual-training curriculum, equipment grants).

### 2. Capitation Realities for Parents

While Free Day Secondary Capitation is budgeted at KES 22,244 per student, actual Treasury quarterly cash disbursements have historically averaged KES 17,000, creating operational deficits in public schools.

reports.title: The Devolution Envelope: How the KES 502B Equitable Share & Conditional Grants Reach 47 Counties
reports.seoTitle: Kenya Devolution Budget 2026/2027: KES 502B CRA Equitable Share Formula | Budget Ndio Story
reports.seoDescription: Detailed guide on how Kenya's KES 502B devolution funds are shared among 47 counties using the CRA 3rd Basis Formula (Population 18%, Health 17%, Agriculture 10%, Poverty 14%).
reports.author: BNS Studios Civic Explainer Desk

provenance.source: Commission on Revenue Allocation (CRA) 3rd Basis Formula & Division of Revenue Act (DORA) 2026

citizenTakeaway: Under Article 202 & 203 of the Constitution, counties are guaranteed an unconditional equitable share of national revenue, set at KES 428B for FY 2026/27.
The CRA 3rd Basis Revenue Sharing Formula distributes funds based on Population (18%), Health Services (17%), Agriculture (10%), Poverty Level (14%), Land Area (8%), and Basic Equal Share (20%).
Additional conditional allocations totaling KES 74 Billion are earmarked for specific national priorities like Community Health Promoters and County Industrial Parks (CAIPs).
The Equalisation Fund distributes KES 9.6 Billion to 14 marginalized arid and semi-arid counties to provide basic water, roads, and electricity.
reports.content:
### 1. The Division of Revenue Architecture

Before counties receive any funds, Parliament passes the **Division of Revenue Act (DORA)**, which divides nationally raised ordinary revenue between the National Government and County Governments.

### 2. The CRA 3rd Basis Allocation Parameters

The Commission on Revenue Allocation distributes the unconditional equitable share among the 47 counties using the following audited parameters:

1. **Basic Equal Share (20%)**: Shared equally across all 47 counties regardless of size.
2. **Population Index (18%)**: Sourced from the official KNBS census.
3. **Health Services Index (17%)**: Sourced from inpatient/outpatient hospital attendance and health facilities.
4. **Poverty Index (14%)**: Poverty gap metric to lift economically disadvantaged regions.
5. **Agriculture Index (10%)**: Value of crop and livestock production per county.
6. **Land Area Index (8%)**: Geographic land size requiring infrastructure.
7. **Road Network Index (8%)**: Maintained road kilometers.
8. **Fiscal Effort & Prudence (5%)**: Reward for counties improving Own-Source Revenue (OSR).

faqs.question: How is the county equitable share calculated in Kenya?
faqs.answer: The Commission on Revenue Allocation (CRA) 3rd Basis formula uses 8 weighted parameters: Basic Equal Share (20%), Population (18%), Health (17%), Poverty (14%), Agriculture (10%), Land Area (8%), Roads (8%), and Fiscal Effort (5%).

faqs.question: What is the difference between Equitable Share and Conditional Grants?
faqs.answer: Equitable Share is unconditional—county assemblies decide how to budget it freely. Conditional grants are earmarked for specific national projects like CAIPs, Universal Health Coverage, or donor-funded climate initiatives.
